original_question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold contain a closed geodesic multinet that does not contain any non-trivial periodic geodesic? Here "closed" means there are no unbalanced (boundary) vertices, and a geodesic multinet is the version of a geodesic net that allows edge multiplicities and self-intersections.
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2.0.1: the open problem asking whether every closed Riemannian manifold contains a closed geodesic multinet not containing a non-trivial periodic geodesic.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact formulation. It correctly captures the universal quantifier over all closed Riemannian manifolds, the sought object being a closed geodesic multinet, the exclusion of any non-trivial periodic geodesic, and the basic gloss that 'closed' means there are no unbalanced/boundary vertices. It also correctly points toward the multinet variant rather than the embedded-net variant.
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem, not as a theorem or conjecture: Section 2, Problem 2.0.1.
Throughout the paper, all geodesic (multi)nets under consideration are assumed to be connected; this convention is implicit in Problem 2.0.1.
A geodesic multinet is finite: it has finitely many vertices and finitely many edges.
Its edges are non-constant geodesic segments between vertices.
In the multinet setting, distinct edges may intersect each other as well as self-intersect; the draft mentions self-intersections but not intersections between different edges.
Each edge carries a positive integer multiplicity.

The balancing condition at a vertex uses the outgoing unit tangent vectors of all incident edges, counted with multiplicity; for a closed geodesic multinet this zero-balance condition holds at every vertex.
To avoid ambiguity, 'closed Riemannian manifold' means compact and without boundary, whereas 'closed geodesic multinet' means the multinet has no unbalanced vertices.
refined_question: Let M be a closed Riemannian manifold (compact and without boundary). Must M contain a connected closed geodesic multinet, i.e. a finite connected immersed multigraph in M whose edges are non-constant geodesic segments between vertices, may intersect or self-intersect, and carry positive integer multiplicities, such that the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors at each vertex is zero when counted with multiplicity (so there are no unbalanced vertices), and such that the multinet contains no non-constant periodic geodesic?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the variational definition in Section 1.1, does every closed Riemannian manifold admit a connected critical point of the length functional on finite immersed multigraphs with no prescribed boundary vertices, whose resulting closed geodesic multinet contains no non-trivial periodic geodesic?
justification: The draft is targeting the exact open problem posed in Section 2. The paper first introduces closed geodesic nets as geodesic nets with no unbalanced vertices, notes that periodic geodesics and unions of periodic geodesics are the simplest examples, and then states verbatim the question in Problem 2.0.1. Section 1.1, especially Definition 1.1.1 and the immediately following conventions, supplies the hidden assumptions needed to make the problem stand-alone: finiteness of the graph, non-constant geodesic edges, positive integer multiplicities in the multinet case, allowance of intersections/self-intersections, the balancing condition at vertices, and the paper-wide convention that only connected geodesic (multi)nets are considered. There is no narrower nearby reformulation that better matches your draft than Problem 2.0.1 itself, so the faithful refinement is to restate that problem with the Section 1.1 definitions made explicit.
